source_type_decision.reason: The source asks for a concrete MySQL/Redis consistency design, including delayed double-delete and binlog listening. A scenario contract is appropriate because the answer must choose a data flow, state consistency boundaries, cover races and failure recovery, and explain operational tradeoffs rather than only describe one mechanism.

primary_sources_checked.title: Redis Docs: Cache-aside
verified_claims: cache-aside reads Redis first, falls back to the primary on a miss, and writes the result back to Redis
updates write the primary and invalidate the cache key
TTL bounds stale-data lifetime and popular-key expiration can create a cache stampede

primary_sources_checked.title: Redis Docs: DEL
verified_claims: DEL deletes one or more keys and ignores non-existent keys
repeated deletion is safe for the cache-key side effect but does not establish distributed exactly-once delivery

primary_sources_checked.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: The Binary Log
verified_claims: binary logging occurs after the statement or transaction completes but before locks are released or commit is done, preserving commit order
InnoDB transactional changes are cached until COMMIT and the entire transaction is written to the binary log before COMMIT executes
binary-log retention must account for downstream consumers that may still need older log files

primary_sources_checked.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual: START TRANSACTION, COMMIT, and ROLLBACK
verified_claims: COMMIT makes the current transaction changes permanent and ROLLBACK cancels them

primary_sources_checked.title: Debezium Documentation: Outbox Event Router
verified_claims: a connector configured with the outbox event router SMT transforms captured outbox-table changes into routed events
the outbox event id can be used for duplicate removal and aggregate id is used as the event key to preserve partition ordering
the documented outbox table behaves as a queue whose changes are expected to be INSERT operations
